The enum is replaced by the string literal 'forbid' in the new model_config, so the import is removed and ConfigDict is added for the new configuration API."}, {"finding_ids": ["app/customers.py:9:config-class"], "search": "    class Config:
        allow_population_by_field_name = True
        anystr_strip_whitespace = True
        extra = Extra.forbid", "replace": "    model_config = ConfigDict(
        populate_by_name=True,
        str_strip_whitespace=True,
        extra="forbid",
    )", "explanation": "The inner `class Config` is deprecated in v2 and is replaced by `model_config = ConfigDict(...)`. `allow_population_by_field_name` maps to `populate_by_name`, `anystr_strip_whitespace` maps to `str_strip_whitespace`, and `Extra.forbid` maps to the string 'forbid'. Behavior is preserved."}, {"finding_ids": ["app/customers.py:19:config-class"], "search": "    class Config:
        allow_mutation = False", "replace": "    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)", "explanation": "The inner `class Config` is deprecated in v2 and is replaced by `model_config = ConfigDict(...)`. `allow_mutation = False` maps to `frozen=True`, which is the inverted equivalent."}], "notes": "Edits cover all three findings. The import edit removes `Extra`, which has no remaining uses, and adds `ConfigDict`. `BaseModel` and `Field` are still used. Behavior note for AuditEntry: in v1, assigning to a field with allow_mutation=False raised TypeError. In v2, frozen=True raises a ValidationError on assignment instead. Callers that catch TypeError on mutation will need updating. No other lines were changed. The Customer `populate_by_name` and `str_strip_whitespace` settings behave the same in v2. Note that `populate_by_name` is still accepted in pydantic 2.x, though newer 2.x releases prefer `validate_by_name`; no change is needed for this migration."}
